title: a `gr.DownloadButton` that lets you download a file with a button click
body:
- [x] I have searched to see if a similar issue already exists.


**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**  
Is possible to directly download file with a button click, rather using the `gr.File` component. Directly download will be more intuitive, and using the gr. File requires two operations.

**Describe the solution you'd like**  
I don't want to add the `gr.File` component on my app's UI. I'd like to download a file (eg: image) from a http url or local path with a button click.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter we don't have a `gr.DownloadButton` component -- we could create a component like this in the future. The other possibility would be to use the `link` attribute of the `gr.Button()` to point to the filepath. Something like this:

```py
import gradio as gr

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    gr.Button(link="/file=cheetah.jpg")
    
demo.launch()
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
In Gradio 4.x, files your local system are not exposed by default, so you'll need to explicitly allow the specific file or directory. E.g. 

```py
import gradio as gr

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
...
    
demo.launch(allowed_paths=["file/material/test.txt"])
```

or you could do a containing folder as well, like:

```py
import gradio as gr

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
...
    
demo.launch(allowed_paths=["file/"])
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: That being said, a `gr.DownloadButton` which takes care of this for you would be a nice logical abstraction to add, so I'll reopen this issue
